name: us-state-tax
description: KANSAS, WHERE THE FIGURE THAT DECIDES A WIDOW'S BILL IS A CHECKBOX: the K-40 has FOUR filing-status boxes and no qualifying-surviving-spouse box, and its head-of-household box qualifies a filer who claimed "Head of Household OR QUALIFYING WIDOW OR WIDOWER WITH A DEPENDENT CHILD" on the federal return - so a Kansas widow is read against the HEAD-OF-HOUSEHOLD column, which is neither the joint one every by-status table defaults to nor the single one a guess reaches for, and three figures turn on it at once: a $6,180 standard deduction against a joint $8,240, a $9,160 exemption PLUS a $2,320 head-of-household additional exemption against a joint $18,320, and the 5.58% band opening at $23,000 rather than $46,000; where a widow with one dependent child and $60,000 of federal AGI owes $2,145.72 and the joint default gives $1,618.24, $527.48 TOO LITTLE because the joint schedule's 5.2% band runs to $46,000 and swallows her whole taxable income, while the single column gives $2,418.86, $273.14 too much - the right answer being BETWEEN the two wrong ones, so no conservative choice of column reaches it; where THAT $2,320 WAS ON THE DEPARTMENT'S FORM A YEAR BEFORE IT WAS IN THE STATUTE, because SB 1 of the 2024 special session said nothing about a head-of-household addition and the 2024 K-40 granted one anyway, and HB 2231 of 2025 then codified it and backdated it to tax year 2024, so a model built from the 2024 statute alone is $2,320 of exemption short in both years; where the same act gives a $2,320 PERSONAL EXEMPTION FOR A STILLBIRTH under 79-32,121(a)(4) from tax year 2025, which nothing models because no return records the fact; where WHAT A KANSAS RETIREMENT COSTS DEPENDS ON WHICH GOVERNMENT EMPLOYED THE RETIREE AND ON NOTHING ELSE - KPERS, the Kansas police, firemen, judges and highway patrol systems, federal civil service and Thrift Savings Plan distributions and military retired pay are subtracted IN FULL with no cap, no age test and no income test, and nothing subtracts a private pension, a 401(k), an IRA or an annuity at any age or below any ceiling, so a single Kansan of 67 with $50,000 of pension pays $0.00 on a government one and $1,942.88 on a private one, and an OUT-OF-STATE public pension is taxed in full because the federal half of the exempt list is 4 U.S.C. 111 and Davis v. Michigan rather than a policy; where KANSAS'S MINIMUM FILING REQUIREMENT CANNOT CHANGE ANYBODY'S TAX, every row of it being exactly that status's standard deduction plus its personal exemption - 26,560 = 8,240 + 18,320, 17,660 = 6,180 + 9,160 + 2,320, 12,765 = 3,605 + 9,160, 13,280 = 4,120 + 9,160 - so the rule is omitted and the four sums are asserted in its place; where Social Security is FULLY EXEMPT from tax year 2024, replacing a cliff that charged $2,845.80 of tax on one dollar of income at $75,000 of federal AGI for a couple with $51,000 of taxable benefits; and where NOTHING IS INDEXED although the bill as introduced would have indexed the standard deduction from 2025, a clause that is not in the act - two brackets at 5.2% and 5.58% doubling at $46,000 on a joint return, a 17% refundable earned income credit cut from 18% in 2013, a 50% child and dependent care credit that is not modelled because no input carries a federal section 21 credit, a food sales tax credit abolished for 2025, and $850 per aged-or-blind box against $700 on a joint return, which is the state's only marriage penalty and has not moved since 1998. Plus 41 states and 1,033 local income taxes across them: New York City, Yonkers, all 24 Maryland jurisdictions, all 92 Indiana counties, all 24 Michigan cities, all 679 municipalities and all 214 Ohio school districts - more taxing jurisdictions than the rest of the United States put together. Zero dependencies, MIT, ESM and CommonJS, TypeScript types included.

scripts.build: rm -rf dist && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.cjs.json && node scripts/finalize.mjs
